la:noun:vetustas.html:
vĕtustas, ātis, f.
id.
,
old age, age, long existence.
Lit.
In gen.: municipium vetustate antiquissimum,: vetustate possessionis se, non jure defendunt,: tantum aevi longinqua valet mutare vetustas,: tum senior: quamvis obstet mihi tarda vetustas; Multaque me fugiant, etc., = senectus,.—Plur.: quae familiarnm vetustatibus aut pecuniis ponderantur,.—
In partic., ancient times, antiquity: historia nuntia vetustatis,: contra omnia vetustatis exempla,: in tantā vetustate non rerum modo sed etiam auctorum,: vetustatem in majus componens,exaggerating, Dietsch: judicio vetustatis,: sic credidit alta vetustas,.—
Transf.
Long duration, great age: quae mihi videntur habitura etiam vetustatem,i.e. will have a long duration,: scripta vetustatem si modo nostra ferent,: vinum in vetustatem servare, till it becomesold, acquires age, : terebinthi materies fidelis ad vetustatem,; ; ; : conjuncti vetustate, officiis, benevolentiā,i. e. long intimacy, ancient friendship,; ; ; .—
Hence, posterity, the remote future (conceived as a time when this age will have become ancient): de me semper omnes gentes loquentur, nulla umquam obmutescet vetustas,: si qua fidem tanto est operi latura vetustas, Ladew. and Forbig. ad loc.; cf.: quis hoc credat, nisi sit pro teste vetustas,.—
In medic. lang.: ulcerum,i. e. inveterate ulcers,; .

la:verb:veto.html:
vĕto, ŭi, ĭtum, 1 (old form vŏto:
votes,: votitus,; cf. ; perf. (poet. and late Lat.) vetavit, : vetati sunt,), v. a.
etym. dub.
, not to suffer a thing to take place, not to permit, to advise against, oppose, forbid, prohibit a thing; and, with a personal object, not to permit one to do a thing, to prevent or hinder him from doing it, not to grant, to forbid him a thing, etc. (syn.: interdico, inhibeo); constr. most freq. with acc. and inf., less freq. with the simple inf., the simple acc., with ut, ne, or the simple subj., or absol.
In gen.
With acc. and inf.: lex peregrinum vetat in murum ascendere,; cf.: quae (lex naturae) vetat ullam rem esse cujusquam, nisi ejus, qui tractare et uti sciat,: ab opere legatos Caesar discedere vetuerat,: rationes a te collectae vetabant, me rei publicae penitus diffidere,: ridentem dicere verum Quid vetat?: non me ulla vetabunt Frigora Parthenios canibus circumdare saltus,: hos vetuit me numerare timor, (3, 27), 4; 2, 32 (3, 30), 8: cum leges duo ex unā familiā non solum magistratus creari vetarent, sed, etc.,: castra ... vallo muniri vetuit,: quae (lex) de capite civis Romani nisi comitiis centuriatis statui vetaret,.—Pass.: cum equites Romani flere pro me edictis vetarentur,: sterni vetabere terrā,: Nolani muros portasque adire vetiti,: redemptoribus vetitis frumentum parare,: ut a praefecto morum Hasdrubal cum eo vetaretur esse,; ; .—
With ut, ne, or the simple subj. (poet.): sive jubebat, Ut faceret quid, Sive vetabat,: edicto vetuit, ne quis se praeter Apellen Pingeret,; : vetabo, qui Cereris sacrum Vulgarit arcanae, sub isdem Sit trabibus,; .—
With quin (ante- and postclass. and rare): nemo hinc prohibet nec votat, Quin quod palam'st venale, emas,; , praef. 17.—
With quominus (rare): at haec (sapientiā) nullā re, quo minus se exerceat, vetari potest,.—
With inf. (poet.): tabulae peccare vetantes,: nec laevus vetet ire picus,: unde proferre pedem pudor vetet,; cf. ; : quid vetat? with a foll. inf., ; ; .—Impers.: ait esse vetitum intro ad eram accedere, (7), 24.—
With acc.
Of the thing: quia bella vetabat,: nec majora veto,: quid jubeatve vetetve, id. M.

11, 493: iter mediis natura vetabat Syrtibus,: tristia damna vetabo,: : solem vetuit Delia tardior,: quercus Phoebum vetat,keeps off,.—Pass.: fossam praeduxit, quā incerta Oceani vetarentur,: (ludere) vetitā legibus aleā,: vetiti hymenaei,: vetitae terrae,: factum vetitum,: vetito ponto,.—

Of the person: cum Graecos facerem Versiculos, vetuit me tali voce Quirinus, etc.,: quos vetat igne Creon,keeps off,.—Pass.: acta agimus: quod vetamur vetere proverbio,; cf.: vetustissimi mortalium nihil per metum vetabantur,: propter eandem causam facere debebimus, propter quam vetamur,: quippe vetor fatis,: mathematici, genus hominum, quod in civitate nostrā et vetabitur semper et retinebitur,.—
Absol.: lex omnis aut jubet aut vetat,: optat supremo collocare Sisyphus In monte saxum; sed vetant leges Jovis,: res ipsa vetat,: a patria pelago vela vetante datis,; .—
In partic.: veto, I forbid it, I protest; the word with which the tribunes of the people declared their protest against any measure of the Senate or of the magistrates, ; ; : ut vim fieri vetarent,.—Of the protest of the praetor against any unlawful measure, ; . —And in the lang. of augury: vetat haruspex,: volucres,: si vetet auspicium,.—Hence, vĕtĭtum, i, n.
That which is forbidden or prohibited, a forbidden or prohibited thing: nitimur in vetitum semper cupimusque negata,: sed jam de vetito quisque parabat opes,: venerem In vetitis numerant,: crebrescit occultis primum sermonibus, ut vetita solent,: agebat quaedam vetita legibus,.—
A prohibition, protest: jussa ac vetita populorum,; : quae contra vetitum discordia?; .

la:adj:vetus.html:
vĕtus, ĕris (ante-class. collat. form of the
nom. sing.vĕter, Enn. and Att. ap. P.; cf. Müll.; abl. regularly, vetere; but veteri,; ; ; ; comp. class. vetustior; archaic form veterior), adj.
Sanscr. vatsas, year; Gr. ἔτος, ϝετος
.
Adj.
Old (opp. young), aged: Acherunticus senex, vetus, decrepitus,: novus amator, vetus puer,: poëta,: veteres ac moris antiqui memores,: veteres et sancti viri, Dietsch: parentes,: pecudes,: gallinae,; : laurus,: caput,. —
Old (opp. new), of long standing: quam veterrumu'st, tam homini optimu'st amicus,: maceria,: Antemna veterior est Romā, Cato ap. P. (Orig. 1, fr. 25): quod si veteris contumeliae oblivisci vellet; num etiam recentium injuriarum memoriam deponere posse?: invidia et infamia non recens, sed vetus ac diuturna,: vetus atque usitata exceptio,: sphaerae illius vetus esse inventum,: amici veteres (opp. novi),: veterrima (amicitia),: naves,: nobilitas,: consuetudo,: provinciae,; .—Esp., of soldiers, veteran, experienced: ille exercitatus et vetus (miles),; cf. exercitus,; ; : copiae,: milites,; : legiones,: centuriones,.—With gen. (post-Aug.): gnaros belli veteresque laborum,: militiae,: regnandi,: scientiae et caerimoniarum,: operis ac laboris,: armorum,.—With inf. (poet.): hinc Fadum petit et veterem bellare Labicum,.—
Old, of a former time (opp. present, existing), former, earlier, ancient, etc. (cf. antiquus): veterem atque antiquam rem novam ad vos proferam,: historia vetus atque antiqua, Brix ad loc.: credendum est veteribus et priscis, ut aiunt, viris,: veterrimi poëtae Stoici,: multo vetustior et horridior ille (Laelius) quam Scipio,archaic, antiquated,: in veterem revoluta figuram,: fama veterum malorum,: injuria,.—
Substt.
vĕtĕres, um, m., the ancients, men of a former time, the fathers, ancestors, forefathers: majores nostri, veteres illi, admodum antiqui, leges annales non habebant,.—Esp., of ancient authors, etc.: nostri veteres,: quae veteres factitarunt,: omnes veteres et Cicero praecipue,; cf. : antiqui veteres,.—
vĕtĕres, um, f. (sc. tabernae), the old booths on the south side of the Forum Romanum (opp. Novae, v. novus): sub Veteribus,; ; .—
vĕtĕra, um, n., the old, old things, antiquity (opp. praesentia): vetera semper in laude, praesentia in fastidio,; cf. : si vetera mihi ignota (sunt),: vetera omittere,to leave out of consideration,: vetera odisse, nova optare,: vetera scrutari,traditions,. —Prov.: vetera vaticinamini, Lorenz ad loc.

la:verb:vetero.html:
vĕtĕro, āvi, ātum, 1, v. a.
vetus
,
to make old (late Lat.): dicendo autem novum veteravit prius,.—P. a.: vĕ-tĕrātus, a, um, old, inveterate: mederi ulceribus veteratis,: caseus,mouldy,.

la:noun:veteres.gloss: the ancients, men of old, forefathers
senses: the ancients, men of old, forefathers

la:adj:vetulus.html:
vĕtŭlus, a, um,
adj. dim. [vetus], little old, old (class.)
Adj.: vetulus, decrepitus senex,: gladiator,: filia,: equi,: arbor (opp. novella),: Falernum,: cornix,; cf. cadi, et saep.—
Substt.
vĕtŭlus, i, m., a little old man, .— Jocularly: mi vetule,my little old fellow,.—
vĕtŭla, ae, f., a little old woman, ; ; .

senses: a corn dolly or small figurine, shaped as an old woman; a term in use among the Druidic pagans of Flanders in the 7th century

la:adj:veteranus.html:
vĕtĕrānus, a, um, adj.
id.
,
old, veteran (in technical lang.): boves,: pecus,: gallinae,: vitis,: mancipia,: hostis,: miles veteranus, or simply veteranus, an old tried soldier, a veteran soldier, a veteran: milites,: veterani,; ; ; ; ; ; cf.: legiones veteranae,i. e. composed of veterans,.—
Trop., experienced, skilled: veteranis manibus libros evolvite,.

la:noun:vetera.gloss: the old; old times, ancient times, antiquity
senses: the old; old times, ancient times, antiquity
la:noun:vetera.html:
Vĕtĕra, um, n.,
a town of Gallia Belgica, now Xanten, ; called also Vetera castra, and 21.

la:adj:vetustus.gloss: that which has existed a long time; old, ancient, aged; established, lasting
senses: that which has existed a long time; old, ancient, aged; established, lasting
after or in the manner of the ancients, old-fashioned, old-time
from ancient times or antiquity; archaic
la:adj:vetustus.html:
vĕtustus, a, um, adj.
vetus
,
that has existed a long time, aged, old, ancient (in the posit. mostly poet., and almost exclusively of things; for the comp. vetustior, v. vetus): veteris vetusti (vini) cupida sum,: templum Cereris,: lucus,: silva,: ligna,: gens,: cornicum saecla,: spatium aetatis,; , cf. : ratio,: res,: opinio,: hospitium,: amicitia,: sors,.—Of a person: vetusto nobilis ab Lamo,.—Comp.: pix,: ova,: memoria,: semen,.—Sup.: sepulcra,: navis,: foedera,: tempora,: instrumentum imperii,ancient records of the State,.—Of persons: qui vetustissimus ex iis, qui viverent, censoriis esset,: auctores,: vetustissimus liberorum. ; ; .—Adv.: vĕtustē. *
After the manner of the ancients, Ascon. ad. ; . —
From ancient times: vetustissime in usu est,.

Absol.: lex omnis aut jubet aut vetat,: optat supremo collocare Sisyphus In monte saxum; sed vetant leges Jovis,: res ipsa vetat,: a patria pelago vela vetante datis,; .—
In partic.: veto, I forbid it, I protest; the word with which the tribunes of the people declared their protest against any measure of the Senate or of the magistrates, ; ; : ut vim fieri vetarent,.—Of the protest of the praetor against any unlawful measure, ; . —And in the lang. of augury: vetat haruspex,: volucres,: si vetet auspicium,.—Hence, vĕtĭtum, i, n.
That which is forbidden or prohibited, a forbidden or prohibited thing: nitimur in vetitum semper cupimusque negata,: sed jam de vetito quisque parabat opes,: venerem In vetitis numerant,: crebrescit occultis primum sermonibus, ut vetita solent,: agebat quaedam vetita legibus,.—
A prohibition, protest: jussa ac vetita populorum,; : quae contra vetitum discordia?; .

la:verb:veto#3.html:
vĕto, ŭi, ĭtum, 1 (old form vŏto:
votes,: votitus,; cf. ; perf. (poet. and late Lat.) vetavit, : vetati sunt,), v. a.
etym. dub.
, not to suffer a thing to take place, not to permit, to advise against, oppose, forbid, prohibit a thing; and, with a personal object, not to permit one to do a thing, to prevent or hinder him from doing it, not to grant, to forbid him a thing, etc. (syn.: interdico, inhibeo); constr. most freq. with acc. and inf., less freq. with the simple inf., the simple acc., with ut, ne, or the simple subj., or absol.
In gen.
With acc. and inf.: lex peregrinum vetat in murum ascendere,; cf.: quae (lex naturae) vetat ullam rem esse cujusquam, nisi ejus, qui tractare et uti sciat,: ab opere legatos Caesar discedere vetuerat,: rationes a te collectae vetabant, me rei publicae penitus diffidere,: ridentem dicere verum Quid vetat?: non me ulla vetabunt Frigora Parthenios canibus circumdare saltus,: hos vetuit me numerare timor, (3, 27), 4; 2, 32 (3, 30), 8: cum leges duo ex unā familiā non solum magistratus creari vetarent, sed, etc.,: castra ... vallo muniri vetuit,: quae (lex) de capite civis Romani nisi comitiis centuriatis statui vetaret,.—Pass.: cum equites Romani flere pro me edictis vetarentur,: sterni vetabere terrā,: Nolani muros portasque adire vetiti,: redemptoribus vetitis frumentum parare,: ut a praefecto morum Hasdrubal cum eo vetaretur esse,; ; .—
With ut, ne, or the simple subj. (poet.): sive jubebat, Ut faceret quid, Sive vetabat,: edicto vetuit, ne quis se praeter Apellen Pingeret,; : vetabo, qui Cereris sacrum Vulgarit arcanae, sub isdem Sit trabibus,; .—
With quin (ante- and postclass. and rare): nemo hinc prohibet nec votat, Quin quod palam'st venale, emas,; , praef. 17.—
With quominus (rare): at haec (sapientiā) nullā re, quo minus se exerceat, vetari potest,.—
With inf. (poet.): tabulae peccare vetantes,: nec laevus vetet ire picus,: unde proferre pedem pudor vetet,; cf. ; : quid vetat? with a foll. inf., ; ; .—Impers.: ait esse vetitum intro ad eram accedere, (7), 24.—
With acc.
Of the thing: quia bella vetabat,: nec majora veto,: quid jubeatve vetetve, id. M.
